newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA RAILWAY SEEKS FUNDS FOR ELECTRIC LINK.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA RAILWAY SEEKS FUNDS FOR ELECTRIC LINK.

text.p: The Bulgarian State Railway (BSR) is seeking funds for the electrification of a link to the Turkish border, its director general said on Wednesday.
Anguel Dimitrov said the U.S. Trade and Development Agency would consider helping the BSR to purchase equipment which could not be produced in Bulgaria, including an optic cable.
The BSR has already received $2 million from the United States through the agency for the construction of a railway to its western neighbour Macedonia.
A Russian firm Zarubezhtransstroi will electrify the 150-km link from the town of Dimitrovgrad to the Kapitan Andreevo checkpoint on the Turkish border, Dimitrov said.
The link's electrification is expected to cost some 2.5 billion levs, he said.

The BSR has renewed work on the electrification of a 35-km link from Sofia to the Dragoman checkpoint on the Serbian border and plans to complete it on December 1. It will cost 500 million levs, Dimitrov said.

The railway will be able to pay its debt of 70 million levs to Varna's Express Bank by the end of the year, Dimitrov said, adding that the BSR owed four billion levs to the state and 800 million levs to the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development.
In a bid to cut spending, the company plans to take a dozen inefficient passenger trains out of service from this month. It has also banned its officials from travelling abroad until the year-end.
Under its restructuring programme, the company will triple its passenger tariffs by 1998 to fill up the gap between the cost of a passenger trip and the cost of a ticket, Dimitrov said.
The BSR will receive a total of $170 million in credits mainly from the World Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, conditional on the restructuring.
